items.title: Bill Phillips Interview, 1961-05-24
items.q: I knew Tubby, yeah. I knew Tubby Hall, and the zoo that used to be down at the place often because we used to have our little portals down here.

ctx.x: And you had one of those overhead then?

I had it then. You see, I used to use it in the studio. And when I come back, there's a fella called Sandsbury, was running it while we left there. And when I come back and look for the overhead trap, I don't know if one of the guys got it out there or what. But I asked Tubby Hall, you might remember? I knew Tubby, yeah. I knew Tubby Hall, and the zoo that used to be down at the place often because we used to have our little portals down here. So I asked Tubby, I said, Tubby, I said, you ever seen my overhead…

items.title: Bill Phillips Interview, 1961-05-24
items.q: I never paid much attention to Tubby.

ctx.x: Anyway, I was going to say Baby Dodds told me once that he learned his press roll partly from Tubby. Yeah, yeah. I'm surprised to hear that, but I never paid much attention to Tubby. Do you remember any press roll that he did?

He could roll, he put them in the middle of the old man Cantrell. Really? He had a tough roll. He made that even, you know, and sound like Tubby man. He had two good wrists. He was tight on the wrist. He was tight on the wrist. And he never would choke his stick that, I mean just like he would choke, try to choke somebody. He let his sticks loose, you know. Just let them go for themselves, because when you test that skin, you got some good skin on that stick, that stick will knock it down if you don't hold it.…
I would have said she was too tight for you, then you can't do nothing.
